clean_prose.in.note: Code, prose and version literals; a scanner that flags any of it is over-matching.

aws_access_key_id.in.note: AWS's own documentation example key — synthetic by construction.

github_token.in.note: Token embedded in a remote URL: the span, not the line, is replaced.

anthropic_api_key.in.note: Pins rule priority: the sk-ant- row must claim the FULL span before the broader sk- shape (the hash is HMAC over the whole sk-ant-… span, so a decoder that lets sk- win produces a different token).

openai_api_key.in.note: The broad sk- shape on a non-Anthropic key.

pem_private_key.in.note: Multi-line BEGIN…END block is ONE span; text after the footer survives.

jwt.in.note: All three JOSE segments are one span; the JWT row outranks the base64 entropy row on the shared eyJ prefix.

high_entropy_hex.in.note: 64 random-looking hex chars over the 3.4 bits/byte floor.

high_entropy_base64.in.note: Base64 run incl. its = padding is one span, over the 4.8 bits/byte floor.

low_entropy_hex.in.note: 64 hex chars of near-zero entropy: shape matches, the randomness test must reject — a decoder without the entropy leg redacts this and diverges.

multi_secret.in.note: Two secrets, two classes: pins the exact substitution count and offset arithmetic after the first replacement changes the buffer length.

repeated_secret.in.note: Equal secrets produce byte-identical tokens under one key — the in-tenant correlation property (04 §7.1) as bytes.

already_redacted.in.note: A previous vector's OUTPUT as input: redaction is idempotent, and the token grammar must never itself match a rule (12 §2.4 prop_redact_idempotent, as a frozen vector).
